p:cNvPr.descr: An illustration depicting a summary of amino acid catabolism. In the middle is the citric acid cycle, made of blue arrows forming a circle. On the top left isocitrate has an arrow pointing up and around to alpha-ketoglutarate in a box. An arrow points from this to succinyl-CoA in a box, which points to succinate. Succinate points to fumarate in a box, which points to malate. Malate points to oxaloacetate in a box, which points to citrate. Citrate points to isocitrate to complete the circle. Above alpha-ketoglutarate is glutamate in a pink box, which points down to alpha-ketoglutarate. Arginin, glutamine, histidine, and proline in a pink box points left to the glutamate mentioned above. Alpha-ketoglutarate points. Isoleucine, methionine, threonine, and valine in a pink box points to succinyl-CoA in a box. Phenylalanine and tyrosine in a pink box points to fumarate in a box. Asparagine and aspartate in a pink box point to oxaloacetate in a box. On the top left and outside of the circle, leucine, lysine, phenylalanine, tryptophan, and tyrosine in a blue box points down to acetoacetyl-CoA in a box, which then points down to acetyl-CoA in a box. An arrow points up and right to ketone bodies from the acetylacetyl-CoA box. To the right of the box is an arrow pointing to citrate in the circle. It also has an arrow pointing right and up to ketone bodies. Isoleucine, leucine, threonine, and tryptophan in a blue box points up to the acetyl-CoA in a box. Alanine, cysteine, glycine, serine, threonine, and tryptophan in a pink box points up to pyruvate in a box. The pyruvate box points left and up to the acetyl-CoA box. It also points right and up to the oxaloacetate box. . CO2 joins this arrow. The oxaloacetate box also has an arrow pointing down and right to glucose. The legend for this image reflects pink as glucogenic and blue as ketogenic.
